data.title: Rep. Casten seeks to curb prediction market insider trading with DOJ whistleblower program
data.description:
Rep. Sean Casten, who could have a top spot in Congress next year, is clamping down on insider trading in prediction markets by incentivizing people to report information anonymously to the Justice Department, amid high-profile incidents involving governmental officials and military personnel.

On Friday, Casten and Rep. Ted Lieu introduced the Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act, which would create a new program at the Justice Department where whistleblowers can report information anonymously about fraud in prediction markets and could potentially be compensated if the information results in a successful enforcement action.

"Prediction markets have a serious insider trading problem, and the current Administration is engaged in corruption of epic proportions," Casten said in a statement. "By encouraging whistleblowers to come forward and report wrongdoing, we can take an important step in cracking down on insider trading to restore accountability and public confidence in the U.S. rule of law."

The news was earlier reported by Politico.

Over the past year, certain bets on prediction markets have drawn scrutiny from both Republicans and Democrats. On Thursday, the Senate passed the "Death Bets Act," which would ban prediction market contracts tied to death, terrorism, assassination and war.

Insider trading on these platforms has also emerged as an ongoing concern, particularly following reports that an active-duty U.S. Army soldier used confidential information to place bets on Polymarket ahead of the capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. Subsequent cases have raised further concerns about government officials exploiting access to nonpublic information for financial gain through prediction markets, including allegations involving the White House's former teleprompter operator.

Political candidates have likewise faced allegations of insider trading on these platforms.

With Democrats now taking control of Congress in January, prediction markets are likely to garner more scrutiny. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., who is slated to chair the Senate Banking Committee, has said she would hone in on prediction markets. On the House side, it is not yet clear who will lead the House Financial Services Committee. Rep. Maxine Waters had been expected to take on that role, but has since been challenged by Casten.

data.title: Simmons issues statement clarifying media reports on Texas multifamily project loan
data.description:
Simmons First National on Friday issued a statement clarifying inaccurate media reports concerning a loan related to a Texas multifamily project.

The company said the loan balance stated in the reports of $133M is incorrect.

The financing provided by Simmons Bank was ~$88M, of which about $44M was participated to another financial institution, all of which is secured by a first lien on the property serving as collateral.

Simmons said the value of the property that serves as collateral to the loan remains well over the outstanding loan balance, with an approximate loan-to-value ratio of 73%.

Simmons Bank does not expect to incur a credit loss on the project.

data.title: Argentina approves incentive scheme for $50.8 billion LNG project
data.description:
Argentina's liquefied natural gas (LNG) project will be included in the country's RIGI investment incentive regime, Energy Minister Luis Caputo said on Friday.

The project - to be developed by Italy's Eni , Argentina's state controlled energy company YPF and Abu Dhabi's XRG - is the largest investment project in Argentina's history, Caputo said in a post on X.

The development hinges on $25 billion of investment between 2027 and 2030, with total investment reaching $50.75 billion by 2050, the minister said, adding that it would enable exports of 12 million tonnes per year of LNG.

"Congratulations to (YPF's CEO) Horacio Marín on this outstanding project, and thanks to the RIGI Committee for its hard work," Caputo wrote.

data.title: Wrapped Monero token crashes 99.8% amid suspected $13.5M exploit
data.description:
A wrapped version of Monero plunged more than 99% on Hyperliquid on Friday after a wallet that received tokens from the deployer account sold approximately $13.5 million worth of the asset, according to blockchain analytics firm Bitquery.

The token, known as XMR1, fell from around $500 to $1 in roughly 30 minutes, a 99.8% decline, according to Bitquery. Wrapped tokens are designed to represent other cryptocurrencies on different blockchains, allowing them to be traded outside their native networks. The collapse affected XMR1 rather than Monero’s native cryptocurrency.

According to Bitquery’s onchain analysis, the wallet received 5.2 million XMR1 tokens from the deployer account before selling approximately $13.5 million worth of the asset on Friday.

The firm traced $13.28 million in USDC transferred to Arbitrum, where $13.22 million was exchanged for 7,467 Ether through CoW Protocol. Most of the ETH was subsequently bridged to Ethereum.

Bitquery also found that proceeds from four hacks earlier in November, involving Across Protocol, Kava, Lighter and Safe, had been used to purchase approximately $6.6 million worth of XMR1, apparently as a route to native Monero. The firm said it found no onchain evidence linking those incidents to Friday’s suspected exploit.

Value of XMR1 purchases linked to funds from four November hacks. Source: Bitquery

Bitquery said its onchain investigation could not establish how the deployer account’s private key was obtained or who controlled it during the transfers, leaving the circumstances of the suspected compromise unconfirmed.

Wagyu operator blames suspected infrastructure breach

PerpetualCow, the pseudonymous operator of Wagyu, the service behind XMR1, attributed the collapse to an alleged breach of hosting provider 1984, claiming that customer data and internal server files had been exposed.

According to PerpetualCow, the XMR1 deployer key had been stored on a server that was subsequently deleted, but the hosting provider allegedly retained logs and files associated with it.

Source: Perpetual Cow

PerpetualCow also pledged to personally reimburse affected traders and said Wagyu would relaunch at a later date, although no timeline was provided.

Cointelegraph contacted the operator for additional details about the suspected breach and reimbursement plans but had not received a response by publication.

data.title: Microsoft emphasizes 'pay-for-performance' in its Azure cloud division: report
data.description:
Microsoft management is emphasizing "pay-for-performance" initiatives for employees in its lucrative Azure cloud business, according to Bloomberg.

Employees who demonstrate better performance will receive more benefits, such as additional stock awards, while those with lower performance results will receive higher scrutiny, according to the report, which cited an internal memo.

"Pay-for-performance only works if we are equally rigorous on both sides: recognizing exceptional impact and being honest when performance falls short," said the memo, which was issued by Arun Ulagaratchagan, executive vice president of Azure.

"Meeting today's bar means closing previous performance gaps and demonstrating a meaningful step-change in impact," he added. "AI is reshaping how the world works, and competition has never been more intense."

"A world-class team like Azure requires world-class talent," a Microsoft spokesperson said, according to the report. "Yesterday, we shared an update to our compensation model in Azure, which includes meaningful additional awards for our strongest performing colleagues. We also shared an update on how we will ensure employees have clear expectations and receive timely, direct feedback from their managers."

Microsoft has focused recently on making the company, which employs more than 220,000 people worldwide, leaner and operate more efficienctly.

Last month, the company began offering a voluntary exit program to eligible employees in the U.S., Canada, India, and the U.K. The buyout program applies to about 60,000 employees. What's more, Azure President Girish Bablani asked senior leaders in his unit to identify ways to reduce costs by at least 20%.

Earlier this year, the company also offered voluntary buyouts to about 7% of its U.S. workforce, or roughly 9,000 employees. Microsoft cut about 4,800 jobs in July, or roughly 2.1% of its global workforce.

data.title: Trump says he still backs Lutnick, urges Nvidia's Huang to apologize
data.description:
US President Donald Trump said on Friday he still supported Howard Lutnick, calling him "a very good businessman" as a scandal at AI chipmaker Nvidia raises questions about Lutnick's handling of Chinese chip sales.

Trump, speaking to reporters at a press conference following his trip to Asia this week, also said he discussed Nvidia's co-founder and now-former CEO Jensen Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping but gave no other details about their conversation.

Reports that Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair with a company executive and ties to a suspected Chinese spy triggered his resignation and sparked investigations by US regulators and the FBI, congressional action, an internal review and a proposed investor class-action lawsuit.

US Senator Tom Cotton, an Arkansas Republican, told the Wall Street Journal earlier on Friday that Lutnick repeatedly ignored warnings that US artificial-intelligence chips were being smuggled to China before the Nvidia scandal became public but stopped short of saying he should resign.

Democrats, who take over Congress in January, meanwhile are probing whether Lutnick used his office to help investment firm Cantor Fitzgerald, which is controlled by his sons, avoid losses stemming from scrutiny of Nvidia's ties to a Chinese firm.

"I have not lost confidence. He's a different kind of a guy, very good businessman," Trump told reporters. "I think he's doing a very good job."

Trump also said he'd like to see the former Nvidia chief "make a big apology and go back," adding: "I did discuss that with President Xi, and he said, 'Oh, brilliant, brilliant — he's a brilliant man.' He is."

His comments contradict those by his Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who told CNBC in an interview earlier on Friday that the former Nvidia CEO did not come up in talks.

The New York Times reported on Friday that the suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang, has extensive ties to China’s defense industry.

Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before the US Senate in a public hearing, an aide to the Senate Banking chairman said on Friday, though a representative for Huang declined to comment. Huang is also scheduled to speak to US House lawmakers behind closed doors in early December.

data.title: Canadian government open to the three-player telecom sector - Globe & Mail
data.description:
The Canadian government is willing to consider takeovers that may reduce the telecom sector to three major companies after Quebecor (QBR. B:CA) () offered to buy Telus () () for around C$31 billion on Monday.

Politicians and civil servants have indicated to industry executives that the government is no longer committed to a four-payer structure and is open to a three-company oligopoly, according to a  Globe & Mail report from Thursday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

The Globe & Mail also reported this week that BCE (), the parent company of Bell Canada, held preliminary discussions with Telus () and hired financial and legal advisers as it explores a potential transaction with the telecom company.

The report on Friday comes after analysts earlier this week downplayed the possibility of a Telus/Quebecor deal, which has the potential to curtail competition in the country. On Monday, BMO cut Quebecor's rating to market perform due to the regulatory risk of a Telus deal.

On Wednesday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney suggested to reporters that fewer providers can still support more competition, in some circumstances, according to a Bloomberg report.

Quebecor () made its C$31B proposal public on Monday, offering Telus () shareholders C$6.35 in cash and 0.17 of a Quebecor () Class B share for each Telus () share. The consideration values Telus () at ~C$19.45 per share, representing a premium of about 60% to its November 13 closing price.

Telus said that the board's special committee's review has identified significant regulatory and execution risks associated with the proposed transaction.
